cyanocitta_cristata: The blue jay can copy the calls of other birds – even birds of prey. It uses them to warn other birds or to chase them away from food.
buceros_bicornis: The female great hornbill walls herself into a tree hole to lay her eggs. The male feeds her and the chicks through a tiny gap.
garrulus_glandarius: A Eurasian jay can hide several thousand acorns. It never finds many of them again – and that helps new oak trees to grow.
alcedo_atthis: The kingfisher catches fish by diving into the water as fast as lightning. A see-through eyelid protects its eyes as it goes in, and it still hits its target.
coracias_caudatus: When it shows off in flight, the lilac-breasted roller dives down and rolls from side to side. With all its colours it looks almost like a flying rainbow.
aptenodytes_forsteri: In emperor penguins, the father keeps the egg on his feet. He warms it under a fold of skin – often for weeks without eating anything.
apteryx_mantelli: The kiwi has its nostrils right at the tip of its beak. It sniffs out food in the ground and can even feel it moving with its beak.
archilochus_colubris: The ruby-throated hummingbird can fly backwards. Its wings move in a figure of eight, so it can also hover in one spot in the air.
fratercula_arctica: A puffin can carry lots of fish in its beak at once. Tiny hooks on its tongue hold them in place. Its beak is only colourful in the breeding season.
pavo_cristatus: The peacock's famous train is not its tail at all! It is made of about 200 long feathers that grow on top of its real tail feathers.
cardinalis_cardinalis: The northern cardinal gets its red colour from its food. When courting, the male feeds the female beak to beak.
balaeniceps_rex: The shoebill can stand completely still for minutes, waiting for prey. Then it snaps it up in a flash with its enormous beak.
